hints: Resolve forces horizontally: the horizontal component of the $20\text{ N}$ string must balance the horizontal component of the string with tension $T$.
Resolve forces vertically: the two vertical tension components support the weight $mg$, so $20\sin 60^\circ + T\sin 45^\circ = mg$ with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
State the equilibrium condition for coplanar forces:
$$\sum F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum F_y = 0$$

Resolve horizontally: the leftward horizontal pull of string $T$ at $45^\circ$ must balance the rightward horizontal pull of the $20\text{ N}$ string at $60^\circ$:
$$T\cos 45^\circ = 20\cos 60^\circ$$
Substitute exact trigonometric values $\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$ and $\cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$:
$$T \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 20 \times \frac{1}{2} = 10$$
Multiply both sides by $2$ and divide by $\sqrt{2}$:
$$T = \frac{20}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.1\text{ N}$$

Resolve vertically: the downward weight $mg$ balances the upward vertical components of both tensions:
$$mg = 20\sin 60^\circ + T\sin 45^\circ$$
Substitute $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, and $T\sin 45^\circ = (10\sqrt{2})\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 10$:
$$10m = 20 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + 10$$
$$10m = 10\sqrt{3} + 10$$
Divide both sides by $10$:
$$m = \sqrt{3} + 1 \approx 1.732 + 1 = 2.73\text{ kg}$$
